tob-4056: The third volume of the Secret Doctrine gathers Blavatsky’s pieces on magic, signs, and the hidden side of the world’s faiths. Put together after her death, it roams from Kabbalah to the rites of old Egypt. Less tidy than the first two volumes, it teems with the startling claims that made her name.
tob-0156: James Darmesteter’s Zend-Avesta is the great French Englishing of Zoroaster’s writ — the hymns, laws, and holy doings of old Persia’s prophet. His foreword and notes brought the Avesta within western scholars’ reach. The work stays a landmark of Iran-learning.
tob-4156: A. P. Sinnett’s Esoteric Buddhism — drawn from the Mahatma Letters — bore Theosophy’s world-system to common eyes in 1883. Its rounds, root-breeds, and veiled masters caught Victorian minds athirst for eastern wisdom. The book launched Theosophy as a folk movement.
arxiv-2605-08856: Rolling a learned model forward step by step — predicting the future — often blows up: small errors amplify into nonsense. Adeel Pervez and Francesco Locatello show that controlling transient amplification tames those blowups and improves long-horizon rollouts. The 2026 paper is about keeping simulated futures on the rails.
arxiv-2605-08956: AI agents that run experiments and write papers sound like the future of science — but are they? Harshit Bisht, Vinay Kumar, Kevin Maik Jablonka, and colleagues argue that today's agentic AI scientists are not built for genuinely autonomous discovery. The 2026 paper is a critical reality check on the hype around robot scientists.
arxiv-2605-09156: Latin nouns had grammatical gender; as Latin became Occitan, the genders shifted in systematic ways. Ahan Chatterjee, Matthias Schöffel, Matthias Aßenmacher, and colleagues explore that shift computationally. The 2026 paper is historical linguistics on a thousand-year grammatical drift.
arxiv-2605-09856: Recovering 3D human meshes from images fails when bodies are occluded — motion priors fill the missing gaps. Tao Tang, Hong Liu, Xinshun Wang, and colleagues incorporate those priors with MoPO. The 2026 paper sees through occlusions using nothing but motion, cleverly.
arxiv-2605-10056: Learning parity with noise — hardness amplification for the sparse LPN problem. Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, and Li Zeyong develop the amplification. The 2026 paper is cryptography on noisy parity. It amplifies cryptographic hardness all the way from weak to strong, provably.
arxiv-2605-10156: Radio galaxy remnants — their afterlife shaped by progenitors and environments: CosmoDRAGoN III. Georgia S.C. Stewart, Stanislav S. Shabala, Patrick M. Yates, and colleagues trace the sculpting. The 2026 paper is radio astronomy on galactic afterlives. It sculpts the afterlife of galaxies.
arxiv-2605-10356: Cortico-cerebellar modularity — the brain's division of labor — as an architectural inductive bias for efficient temporal learning. Alexandra Voce, Emmanouil Giannakakis, and Claudia Clopath propose it. The 2026 paper is brain-inspired AI. It learns temporal patterns the way brains do.
arxiv-2605-10556: Energy models for multimodal LLM inference serving — interpretable and closed-form: EnergyLens. Vittorio Palladino, Gianluca Palermo, and colleagues derive the models. The 2026 paper is green AI. It predicts inference energy without a black box. EnergyLens sees the watts. Green AI, measured precisely.
pmc-13454356: LILRB4 identified as a regulator of M2c macrophages and a potential immunotherapeutic target in ovarian cancer. Huijuan Zhou, Qing Zhang, Bo Yin, and colleagues make the discovery. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cancer immunology. It nominates a new immune target for ovarian tumors.
pmc-13453756: Amateur padel players with ankle sprains — their functional outcomes and rehabilitation behaviors, studied cross-sectionally. Faris Alanazi, Hussain Saad Al Dera, Thamer Al Shammary, and colleagues survey the players. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is sports medicine. It asks how padel players recover from sprains.
pmc-13458356: Traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine on X, formerly Twitter, from 2015 to 2024 — mapped and analyzed. Jahinna Duplaix, Sébastien Abad, Marion Bruna, and colleagues mine the posts. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is digital health communication. It tracks a decade of alternative medicine tweets.
pmc-13461556: Human astrocytes under inflammatory and immune stimuli — a candidate recurrent inflammatory signature revealed by integrated meta-analysis of their transcriptomes. Andrea Luque-Bolivar, Karem Ruiz-Araujo, and colleagues meta-analyze. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is glial biology. It finds astrocytes' shared alarm signal.
pmc-13451856: Periodontal disease inflammation — mitigated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Raza Ali Naqvi, Araceli Valverde, Salvador Nares, and colleagues uncover the mechanism. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is periodontal immunology. It finds immune suppressors calming gum disease. Periodontal inflammation, mitigated. Suppressor cells work.
pmc-13591656: Aqueous zinc batteries — made efficient by an angstrom-scale confined ion sieve and accelerator. Xing Peng, Caichao Ye, Yingqiang Li, and colleagues build the sieve. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is battery science. It sieves ions at the atomic scale. Batteries, improved.
pmc-13509456: Osteosarcoma's coagulome-immune crosstalk — the C3-C3AR1 axis revealed as a candidate mediator by integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. Jianhua Mu, Yitian Wang, Han Liu, and colleagues do the integration. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is osteosarcoma. It links clotting and immunity in bone cancer.
arxiv-2606-16956: Algebraists Radford Green, Cornell Holmes, and Mee Seong Im study multisymmetric polynomials, symmetric functions in several sets of variables, acting on set-theoretic quiver representations, combinatorial models built from directed graphs. The paper uncovers how these polynomials organize the representations' structure. It extends classical invariant theory into the world of quivers.
arxiv-2606-17056: Nick Jiang, Isaac Kauvar, and Jack Lindsey discover that language models carry an internal value axis, a direction in their activations that tracks whether they are on the right track. The paper shows this signal predicts correctness before the model finishes answering. The finding opens new ways to catch AI mistakes as they happen.
arxiv-2606-17156: Styliana Grigoriou and colleagues watch blazars, galaxies with jets aimed at Earth, in polarized light and gamma rays at once. They find that swings in optical polarization track gamma-ray outbursts, linking the two to the same violent jet events. The correlation helps pin down where in the jet the highest-energy light is born.
arxiv-2606-17456: Xi Chu and YuPeng Hou expose incumbent advantage in LLM recommendation systems: famous brands get pushed regardless of merit. Brand bias and cognitive manipulation dynamics steer users toward the familiar. The paper documents the effect and its mechanisms, a warning for AI-mediated shopping.
arxiv-2606-17656: H. Sugama derives Schrödinger equations and fluctuation theorems for collisionless plasma systems. The quantum-like equations describe classical plasmas, and the theorems constrain their fluctuations. The work bridges plasma physics and statistical mechanics. The theorems constrain how far plasmas can stray from equilibrium.
arxiv-2606-17856: Bihao Zhan and colleagues synergize explicit reasoning via frequency-aware multi-granularity graph flow in FlowRAG. The retrieval system reasons over knowledge graphs at multiple scales, weighting frequencies that matter. The approach makes RAG both smarter and more transparent. Benchmarks on multi-hop question answering show clear gains over standard retrieval pipelines.
arxiv-2606-18256: Yoonseok Oh and colleagues generate dynamic in-group personas to enhance human-AI rapport. The AI adopts a persona that feels like one of us, shifting with the conversation. Rapport makes people trust and use AI assistants more. The work studies the psychology of synthetic companionship.
plos-pone-0003456: Geneticists proposed a bold origin story for split genes in this 2008 paper. Eukaryotic genes are chopped into coding pieces separated by long non-coding stretches, and nobody knew why. The authors argued this fractured architecture could have arisen from random genetic sequences, offering a fresh hypothesis for one of molecular biology's oldest puzzles.
plos-pone-0003556: Neuroscientists Semir Zeki and John Paul Romaya scanned the brain on hate in this landmark 2008 study. Seventeen volunteers viewed faces of people they hated while lying in an fMRI scanner, and the team mapped the neural correlates of the emotion. The brain's hate circuit overlapped partly with romantic love's, suggesting passion's dark twin runs on neighboring machinery.
plos-pone-0003656: In 2008, a team showed a gene silencer shaping the growing brain. The protein REST, known for switching off neuron genes outside the brain, was found steering the mesh around cells as neurons form. By tuning that outer scaffold, REST helps guide stem cells into becoming neurons.
plos-pone-0003756: In 2008, Krintel, Osmark, and Larsen pinpointed the switches on a fat-burning enzyme. Two serine spots, 649 and 650, proved to be the main controls for protein kinase A activation of hormone-sensitive lipase. The precise mapping shows exactly where the body flips its fat-release switch.
plos-pone-0003856: In 2008, a team found exercise tuning the brain's hunger signals. Physical activity boosted how the brain's AMPK and mTOR energy sensors respond to leptin, the satiety hormone. The result shows exercise rewiring appetite control at the molecular level, not just burning calories.
plos-pone-0003956: In 2008, Eckmeier, Geurten, and Kress tracked how finches aim their eyes in flight. Free-flying zebra finches used gaze strategies tuned to optic flow. The study reveals the visual steering behind a bird's darting flight.
plos-pone-0004056: In 2008, Benn, Fisker, and Rodrigues found a birth vaccine acting differently by sex. Oral polio vaccine given with BCG at birth shifted infant mortality by sex. In Guinea-Bissau, the sex-differential effect challenged one-size-fits-all vaccine schedules. The surprising finding urges sex-aware design in newborn immunization programs.
plos-pone-0004156: In 2009, Watson, Ghodasra, and Platt linked a gene to monkey manners and moods. Serotonin transporter variants shaped social reward and punishment in rhesus macaques. Gene type tuned how monkeys valued social cues. The primate result echoes human social genetics closely.
plos-pone-0004256: In 2009, Sabado, Kavanagh, and Kaufmann replayed HIV's first strike in a dish. Lab priming recreated HIV-1-specific T cell responses seen in patients. The dish model showed fast loss of virus reactivity over time. The neat system speeds vaccine testing greatly.
plos-pone-0004356: In 2009, Pérez-Berná, Pabst, and Laggner probed viral membranes with short peptides. A peptide library was screened by DSC and SAXD against hepatitis C proteins directly. The heat and X-ray data matched the biology. The neat screen maps membrane-active regions well.
plos-pone-0004456: In 2009, Lehnert, Van Loo, and Thilakarathne linked genome parasites to gene tuners. Evidence for co-evolution between human microRNAs and Alu repeats was found. The jumping genes and tiny RNAs shaped each other. The finding illuminates genome history. The repeats are highly abundant.
plos-pone-0004556: In 2009, Yang, Tang, and Huang mapped a virus's wake-up switch. RTA promoter demethylation and histone acetylation regulated murine gammaherpesvirus reactivation. The epigenetic marks flipped the sleeping virus awake. The finding maps viral latency control. The viral balance is delicate indeed.
plos-pone-0004656: In 2009, Striegl, Roske, and Kümmel solved a Golgi protein's odd shape. An unusual armadillo fold in vesicular transport factor p115 was revealed. The structure explained Golgi tethering well. The finding maps cell logistics anew. The protein fold is unusual.
plos-pone-0004756: In 2009, a team found muting PINK1 wrecking cell power anew here today. Muting PINK1 hurt cell DNA and energy making. The dopamine cells suffered quite badly here. The study maps Parkinson's harm well. The cell breakdown is deep indeed here.
plos-pone-0358756: Flatworms can regrow a lost head, so scientists have wondered whether memories could survive the process. This paper reports a failure: repeated attempts to teach two flatworm species a simple learned response did not work, despite careful methods and historical precedent. The authors publish the negative result openly, arguing that failed experiments deserve a place in science — they stop others from repeating the same dead end.
plos-pone-0358056: Studying the eye’s pigment cells needs a steady supply — and sheep eyes are cheap and plentiful. This paper showed how to isolate uveal melanocytes from ovine eyes and grow them in 2D and 3D culture. The method gives eye researchers an accessible model for studying melanoma and eye disease.
plos-pone-0358356: Aging well takes more than doctor visits — it takes community. This study protocol laid out a trial evaluating community-based integrated care for functional decline and quality of life in middle-aged and older adults. Publishing the protocol first ensures the eventual results will be judged against a fixed plan.
plos-pone-0357156: Phone cameras bracket exposures to capture bright skies and dark shadows — then must fuse them cleanly. MEF-TBN is a three-branch neural network for multi-exposure image fusion that extracts features and enhances color. The approach produces sharper, more natural composite photos than older fusion methods.
plos-pone-0358556: A trained attendant at birth can mean the difference between life and death — yet many Bangladeshi mothers still deliver without one. This paper combined classic statistics with machine learning to map the prevalence and drivers of skilled birth attendance in Bangladesh. The findings point policymakers to the levers that actually get trained help to mothers.
plos-pone-0350956: Cancer survivors often face crushing loneliness after treatment ends. This paper published the protocol for a pilot trial testing an adapted social prescribing intervention — connecting survivors to community — against usual care. The feasibility pilot will show whether prescribing social life can heal what medicine leaves behind.
plos-pone-0355956: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency leaves lungs vulnerable to bronchiectasis — permanently widened airways. This study validated the Bronchiectasis Severity Index in these patients. The validated score gives doctors a tested tool for predicting who will fare worst.
plos-pone-0346756: Blood pooling between brain and skull can return after surgery. This paper used machine learning to classify recurrence risk after surgical treatment of chronic subdural hemorrhage. The model flags high-risk patients for closer follow-up.
plos-pone-0354756: Marbled pork tastes better — and Chinese and Western pigs marble differently. This integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis identified divergent regulatory networks for intramuscular fat in the two pig types. The networks reveal the molecular recipes behind marbling, guiding breeders.
plos-pone-0358456: Future sport managers need communication skills — and entrepreneurial drive to match. This paper tested career awareness as a mediator between communication skills and entrepreneurial tendencies in prospective sport managers. The mediation model shows how self-knowledge turns the ability to talk into the ability to build enterprises.
plos-pone-0357756: Newborns lose body heat dangerously fast — and mothers’ everyday practices decide survival. This qualitative descriptive study explored preventive practices against newborn hypothermia among post-natal mothers in Kilimanjaro’s public health facilities. The findings guide warming interventions that fit real mothers’ lives.
plos-pone-0355056: Sequencing short synthetic DNA strands quickly accelerates synthetic biology. OligoSeq enables rapid nanopore sequencing of single-stranded oligonucleotides. The streamlined method turns around oligo reads fast enough to keep pace with high-throughput DNA synthesis.
plos-pone-0354456: Acute myeloid leukemia urgently needs new drugs — and computation can accelerate the hunt. This paper prepared AML proteins for in silico drug design using pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. The computational pipeline shortens the road from protein structure to drug candidate.
plos-pone-0356356: Software developers handle personal data daily — but what makes them comply with privacy rules? This paper examined how legal awareness shapes developers’ data compliance behavior through a deterrence theory lens. The findings reveal that fear of punishment matters less than believed — with implications for how companies actually achieve compliance.
plos-pone-0343756: Cowpea — black-eyed pea — feeds millions, yet its varieties need genetic fingerprinting. This paper developed KASP molecular markers and constructed a fingerprinting system based on ddRAD sequencing. The genetic toolkit lets breeders and seed systems verify varieties — protecting farmers from mislabeled seed.
plos-pone-0355856: Children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia breathe the same polluted air as everyone else — with deadlier consequences. This Northern Thailand study linked air pollution to mortality in ALL patients across age groups from 1999 to 2020. The two-decade analysis adds childhood cancer to air pollution’s ledger of harm.
plos-pone-0356056: Frankincense trees — Boswellia sacra — are overharvested and poorly mapped. This paper combined spectral signature mapping with deep learning detection using WorldView-3 satellite imagery. The space-based census gives conservationists the first accurate maps of these culturally precious, ecologically threatened trees.
plos-pone-0355556: ‘Sexual harassment definitely involves a hierarchical transgression’ — European experts’ blunt framing. This paper analyzed key informants’ discourses on sexual harassment in European universities. The expert perspectives reveal how power — not just behavior — defines harassment in academic hierarchies.
plos-pone-0354856: Getting to cancer screening — transportation — shapes when cancer gets found. This scoping review examined transportation-related factors, screening, and stage at diagnosis. The findings expose how bus routes and car ownership quietly determine whether cancer is caught early or late.
plos-pone-0355156: Fetal growth restriction can starve babies of oxygen — and cord blood S100B might flag it. This prospective cohort study evaluated the protein’s concentration as a biomarker of fetal hypoxia in late growth restriction. The findings could give obstetricians a molecular alarm for babies in silent distress.
plos-pone-0352856: Therapists assessing motor function with an app — what helps and what hinders? This qualitative study of the MFM-Play app examined barriers and levers to its hospital use. The findings guide digital health designers toward tools therapists will actually adopt at the bedside.
plos-pone-0341756: Blood cancer patients in Thailand need social support measured in their own language. This paper tested the psychometric properties of the Thai version of the Illness-Specific Social Support Scale Short Version-8 among hematological malignancy patients. The validated scale gives Thai oncology teams a trustworthy window into patients’ support networks.
plos-pone-0354156: Iris persica — wild Persian irises — vary phenotypically across accessions. This paper revealed those variations with multivariate analysis. The characterized diversity preserves knowledge of wild irises — beautiful and genetically valuable — before habitats vanish.
plos-pone-0354256: Diabetic wounds in Duhok, Iraq — Pseudomonas aeruginosa lurking in them. This paper measured prevalence and risk factors. The findings guide wound care where resistant bacteria threaten limbs — and lives.
plos-pone-0351756: Fat talk — ‘I’m so fat’ rituals among friends — corrodes body image in Chinese female nursing students. This paper examined that relationship with self-acceptance as mediator. The mediation analysis revealed how casual body-bashing erodes self-worth. The findings matter doubly — these students will counsel patients on health while battling their own body demons. The research points to self-acceptance as the intervention target.
plos-pone-0354356: Person-centred leadership — in health and social care — developed through education. This paper captured leaders’ experiences following such a programme. The qualitative accounts revealed how training reshaped leadership practice. The findings show person-centredness cascading — leaders who experience it deliver it to staff and patients.
plos-pone-0352256: Specialized machine translation — fine-tuning strategies compared: textual overlap versus domain alignment. This paper did so for LLMs. The findings revealed what actually adapts language models to specialties — matching words or matching worlds. The research guides the efficient customization of translation AI.
plos-pone-0353956: Diabetes drugs and osteoarthritis risk — SGLT2 inhibitors versus GLP-1 receptor agonists. This multi-institutional cohort compared their effects. The findings suggested metabolic drugs influence joint degeneration. The research adds an unexpected dimension to diabetes prescribing — joints as well as glucose.
plos-pone-0353556: Shock at ICU admission — its prognostic impact in acute respiratory failure. This paper quantified it. The findings showed circulatory collapse compounding breathing failure predicts death. The research sharpens triage — identifying the respiratory patients whose hearts are also failing.
plos-pone-0353856: Newborns in pain — their brain activity synchronizing with mothers’ during skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding, and lullabies. This paper measured that synchrony. The findings revealed parent-led soothing as neural coupling — two brains, one rhythm. The research validated what mothers always knew — presence as analgesia.
plos-pone-0353056: Wild tigers in Nepal’s Central Zoo — their captive behavior documented. This paper observed it. The ethological record revealed how the wild adapts — or fails to — behind bars. The findings informed captive welfare — the tiger’s mind, considered.
plos-pone-0353756: Plant-rich foods — consumers’ purchase intentions and healthy eating — driven by internal and external leading variables. This pilot study examined those impact mechanisms. The analysis revealed what nudges shoppers toward greener diets. The findings informed the marketing — and policy — that could shift eating patterns at scale.
plos-pone-0353456: Hospitalized COVID-19 patients — serum albumin and blood urea as independent in-hospital mortality predictors. This retrospective cohort demonstrated it. The findings turned routine labs into death forecasts. The research armed the clinicians — the simple blood test as triage. The independence claim is the strength: both markers predicted death even after adjusting for age, comorbidities, and severity.
plos-pone-0352456: Wild male red deer — season and antler growth effects on carcass traits and meat quality. This paper studied the selectively stalked harvest. The findings linked the rut to the table. The research served the game management — venison quality, by season.
plos-pone-0352756: US hospitals — patient satisfaction’s association with hospital quality. This paper explored it. The findings tested whether happy patients mean good care. The research questioned the metric — the smile as quality’s proxy. The association question is the accountability: it asks whether the patient-experience industry measures anything real.
plos-pone-0353156: Video object segmentation — consistent — via uncertainty-aware memory propagation. UAMP is that method. The findings tracked objects through frames, knowing its doubts. The research advanced the video AI — the segmentation that remembers, and hesitates. The uncertainty awareness is the honesty: the model propagates its confidence alongside its masks, flagging shaky frames.
plos-pone-0353356: Power transformer bushing insulation failure — mapped via frequency response analysis and electrostatic simulation. This paper did so. The findings located the failing insulation. The research protected the grid — the transformer’s weak point, found. The electrostatic simulation is the complement: it predicts where the field concentrates, guiding where to look for failure.
plos-pone-0352156: India’s caesarean epidemic — is the private sector to blame? This multivariate analysis of the National Family Health Survey asked. The findings apportioned the blame. The research informed the obstetrics — the surgical birth’s economics, exposed. The private-sector question is the controversy: it tests whether profit motives are driving unnecessary surgeries.
plos-pone-0352356: Cancer screening questions — reliability tested from the National Health Interview Survey. This paper evaluated them. The analysis asked whether the survey’s questions measure consistently. Its value is the nation’s cancer data. The work validates the questions behind the statistics.
plos-pone-0351956: Charlson comorbidity analytics — a population strategy identifying hospitalization risk, repeat admissions, and high cost. This paper built it. The analysis stratified the population by the classic index. Its management value is the targeting. The work finds the costly, before the cost.
plos-pone-0345056: Zambian TB patients on treatment — mortality predictors in a rural general hospital retrospective cohort. This paper identified them. The analysis asked who dies despite treatment. The finding targets the vulnerable. The work finds the fatal gaps in the rural TB program.
europmc-pmc2807856: Dirty air sends people to the ER, and this 2009 study pins down why they come. The team tied daily soot and its chemical parts to ER visits for each cause. Harm was not the same across ills. The split gives rule-makers proof for curbing the worst kinds of grime.
europmc-pmc2815756: Could short fasts make cancer treatment work better? This 2009 case series reports on patients who fasted around their chemotherapy sessions. The authors describe the cases and the rationale: fasting may protect healthy cells while sensitizing tumors. The early report was provocative rather than conclusive. It launched serious research into fasting as a companion to cancer therapy.
europmc-pmc2829056: A test's ROC curve measures its accuracy, but what does the area under it mean genetically? This 2010 paper works out the genetic interpretation of the area under the ROC curve in genomic profiling. The authors connect a statistics workhorse to genetics. Their framework helps researchers judge what genomic predictions can realistically achieve.
europmc-pmc2848556: A germ tenant in mosquitoes can bar dengue. This 2010 paper shows the lodger germ Wolbachia arms Aedes aegypti against the dengue virus. The team proves the guard in caged trials. The find loosed a keen living weapon against a virus with no cure.
europmc-pmc2868856: Risk numbers can wobble with study design, and this 2010 paper probes how much. The authors compare relative risk estimates from studies of the same population with different response rates and designs. Their probe quantifies the wobble. The work warns epidemiologists to mind their methods.
europmc-pmc2970556: The brain's immune cells prune synapses, guided by what eyes see. This 2010 paper shows microglial interactions with synapses are modulated by visual experience. The authors' imaging catches the pruning. Their work links experience to brain wiring. Dark-reared mice kept messier connections.
europmc-pmc3000156: A winter virus puts kids in hospital, this 2003 study finds. The authors report metapneumovirus infections among hospitalized children. Their work confirmed the germ as a real threat. The study guided testing. It ranks just behind RSV in tiny lungs. Winter wards brace for its return.
europmc-pmc3102656: Plant ID got a DNA guide. This 2011 paper helps researchers choose and use plant DNA barcodes. The authors weigh the gene candidates. Their guide steadied plant identification. Two genes beat one, they find. Herbaria now barcode new specimens. The guide is freely available online.
europmc-pmc3141456: A well-being scale got tested on teens. This 2011 paper validates the Warwick-Edinburgh scale for teenage students. The authors confirm it works for adolescents. Their work guides school surveys. The scale asks fourteen simple questions. Schools now track pupil well-being yearly.
europmc-pmc3149556: U.S. HIV infections got counted. This 2011 paper estimates HIV incidence in the United States for 2006 to 2009. The authors reveal stable numbers. Their work guides prevention. Fifty thousand new cases hit yearly. Gay men bore the heaviest burden. The numbers guided funding decisions.
europmc-pmc3237356: Womb pesticide exposure dimmed young minds. This 2011 study links prenatal bug-spray exposure to weaker childhood thinking. The authors reveal the effect. Their work pushed regulation. Test scores fell with higher doses. Farmworker families faced the most risk. The study shaped safety rules.
europmc-pmc3253456: Mercury poisoning got a treatment review. This 2012 paper surveys mercury's harms and how to treat them. The author grades the options. Their overview guides doctors. Chelation drugs lead the treatments. Fish eaters face the most risk. The review is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3266256: Childhood hardship left gene marks. This 2012 paper links early adversity to stress-gene methylation in adults. The authors reveal the marks. Their work lights up trauma research. The marks persisted for decades. Therapy research cites the finding. Tyrka's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3283556: Malaria drugs got a life-cycle test. This 2012 paper tests current malaria drugs across parasite life stages. The authors reveal the gaps. Their work guides drug use. Few drugs killed liver stages. The test standardized drug screening. Delves's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3323356: Motivation theory met health. This 2012 paper applies self-determination theory to health behavior. The authors map the fit. Their overview guides counselors. Autonomy drove change, they found. Patrick's review is widely cited. It shaped counseling practice. The review is a classic.
europmc-pmc3325956: Mouse cycles got a photo guide. This 2012 paper offers photos for staging mouse estrous cycles. The authors provide the images. Their work spread through labs. Byers's team led the work. The guide is open access. Labs adopted it widely. The tool is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3420456: Schizophrenia got a gender review. This 2012 paper reviews how schizophrenia differs in men and women. The authors map the differences. Their overview guides psychiatry. Ochoa's review is widely cited. It is a classic. It shaped treatment. The review is widely taught.
europmc-pmc3435256: Vivax malaria got a 2010 world map. This 2012 paper maps vivax malaria across the globe. The authors reveal the map. Their work guides control. Gething's team led the work. The paper is a landmark. It is widely cited. It shaped eradication plans.
europmc-pmc6510456: Reading the full DNA of bacteria has let scientists watch drug-resistant germs evolve and spread almost in real time. This review shows how genome sequencing traces outbreaks, reveals how resistance genes move, and explains why some superbugs now defeat every drug doctors have. It is a tour of the genomic tools that hospitals use to fight back against untreatable infections.
europmc-pmc6611156: Pericytes - the shy cells hugging capillary walls - turn out to be key stagehands of brain blood flow. Known since the 1870s but long ignored, they regulate vessel tone, guard the blood-brain barrier, and falter in stroke and dementia. This review restores these wallflowers to their starring vascular role.
europmc-pmc6616856: Antibiotics do not vanish after use - they wash into rivers, soils, and farms, breeding resistance in the wild. This review traces antibiotic pollution from microbial ecology to public policy: how environmental drug residues select for superbugs and what rules could stem the flow. The fix needs ecologists and lawmakers together.
europmc-pmc6656856: Tiny RNA messengers circulate in blood - remarkably stable - and cancers leave their signature in them. This review weighs circulating microRNAs as cancer biomarkers: their promise for early detection and the hurdles, from noisy measurements to unclear origins. Liquid biopsy via microRNA is promising but unfinished.
europmc-pmc6688256: Flavonoids - the pigments behind autumn leaves and berry blues - are ancient plant inventions. Tracing their metabolism's evolution, this review shows how plants built the flavonoid toolkit over deep time. The story explains why these compounds are everywhere in the plant kingdom.
europmc-pmc6704256: Alzheimer's plaques may need microglia - the brain's immune cells - to take root. Wiping out microglia with a CSF1R-blocking drug, researchers watched plaque development stall in an Alzheimer's mouse model. The finding flips the script: the brain's defenders may unwittingly nurture the very plaques they surround.
europmc-pmc6723656: Yogurt, kimchi, kefir - fermented foods are having a moment. This review defines what counts as fermented, how these foods shift gut microbes, and what that means for digestion. The hype is real but uneven: some benefits are solid, others still need proof.
europmc-pmc6737756: Patients are research partners, not just subjects - but involving them well takes more than good intentions. This systematic review gathered frameworks for patient and public involvement in research, then co-designed a pilot putting them to the test. The result is practical guidance for making involvement real.
europmc-pmc6769656: Blood vessels are lined with living wallpaper - endothelial cells that do far more than contain blood. This update reviews vascular endothelial biology: how the cells regulate flow, clotting, and inflammation. The single-cell layer turns out to be a command center for circulation.
europmc-pmc6790056: Single-cell RNA sequencing samples each cell once - no reruns possible. MetaCell tackles the noise by grouping similar cells into robust 'metacells' via K-nearest-neighbor graphs. The method turns shaky single-cell snapshots into trustworthy portraits.
europmc-pmc6822756: Science studies itself now - mapping fields with data and pictures. This paper offers a method for careful scientometric reviews: charting a research field's structure, trends, and turning points. The maps make the literature easy to explore. A field guide to the fields themselves.
europmc-pmc6857056: The body's own bubbles make perfect drug runners. This review tours cell-made vesicle drop-off systems for cancer: homemade packages hauling medicine to tumors.
